title: Diego G. Campos
text:
Diego G. Campos



Associate Professor


Knowledge Centre for Education (KSU) · University of Stavanger, Norway


Email Google Scholar ORCID OSF GitHub LinkedIn Bluesky

:::



I develop and evaluate novel methodological approaches to research synthesis to improve the efficiency, transparency, and policy relevance of systematic reviews and meta-analyses. My work focuses on meta-analysis and individual participant data meta-analysis (IPD-MA), and their application to the study of educational inequalities. I examine how individual, family, and school factors shape educational outcomes, with a particular interest in digital competence and other key competencies for learning and participation in modern societies. I also develop AI-assisted tools to make systematic evidence syntheses more efficient, transparent, and reproducible.






2026 — Three book chapters in press in Studying Educational Inequality from a Longitudinal Perspective (eds. Hansen, Klapp & Rolfe), including a chapter on family income dynamics and academic outcomes in Norway.


2026 — New paper in Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science: Fast-Track Your Abstract Screening: Mastering ASReview


2026 — New paper in Learning and Individual Differences: AI tools for systematic literature reviews and meta-analyses in educational psychology


2025 — Awarded the H.M. Kongens Gullmedalje (The King’s Gold Medal) for the PhD thesis Approaches to Integrating Large Data into Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses in Education.


2025 — Awarded the GEBF Junior Publication Prize by the Society for Empirical Educational Research.


2024–2028 — Work Package Coordinator for MapIE (Mapping of Longitudinal Data of Inequalities in Education), EU Horizon Europe grant (€2,999,644.75).

title: Research
text: My research sits at the intersection of methodology and educational science. I develop and apply advanced quantitative methods to study educational inequalities and the factors that shape learning outcomes.

title: Research
text:
Current Projects

Statistical Methods for Research Synthesis
I develop statistical methods for research synthesis, with a focus on complex educational data and evidence integration. My research includes individual participant data meta-analysis, methods for synthesizing data from large-scale assessments, approaches for handling effect-size dependencies, and the application of machine learning to evidence synthesis.


Mapping of Longitudinal Data of Inequalities in Education (MapIE)
As part of the EU-funded MapIE project (https://mapie-project.eu/home), we examine the mechanisms through which individual pupil-level characteristics contribute to educational inequalities across Europe. Our research focuses on understanding how these factors influence educational outcomes and on assessing the capacity of policies and practices to compensate for such disparities. By analyzing educational systems at the school, regional, and national levels, we aim to generate evidence that can inform more equitable and effective educational policies.


AIRES — AI-Assisted Research Synthesis in Educational Sciences
I am developing AIRES (AI-Assisted Research Synthesis), a research program focused on integrating artificial intelligence into evidence synthesis workflows in the educational sciences. The project aims to make systematic reviews and other forms of research synthesis more efficient, transparent, and reproducible by combining rigorous review methodology with advances in machine learning and large language models.


Educational Inequalities
I examine the factors that shape students’ educational outcomes and the development of competencies that are essential for learning and participation in modern societies. Using large-scale national and international assessments, as well as linked administrative register data, I investigate how individual characteristics, family background, school environments, and broader contextual conditions contribute to educational inequalities and differences in student achievement.
